original_question: Is a cubic fourfold X rational if and only if its Kuznetsov component Ku(X) is equivalent to the bounded derived category of a K3 surface?
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Conjecture 3.16 (Kuznetsov), which the survey explicitly presents as the relevant restatement of [80, Conjecture 1.1]. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact logical shape of the target statement: it asks whether rationality of a cubic fourfold X is equivalent to the condition that its Kuznetsov component Ku(X) be equivalent to the bounded derived category of a K3 surface. That is essentially Conjecture 3.16 as written in the paper. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s local meaning of cubic fourfold is a smooth cubic hypersurface X ⊂ P^5. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

The ambient field should be specified: throughout the paper varieties are over an algebraically closed field K, and in Section 3.4 the standing assumption is char(K) ≠ 2. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

Ku(X) should be defined, not merely named: it is the admissible subcategory in the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H), O_X(2H)⟩, where H is the hyperplane class. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

The existential quantifier on the K3 side should be explicit: there exists a K3 surface S over K such that Ku(X) is equivalent to Db(S), the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on S. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the type of equivalence should be made explicit as an exact K-linear triangulated equivalence. The conjecture itself does not add Fourier–Mukai or degree-shift compatibility assumptions. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

The paper’s nearby Remark 3.17 makes clear that the conjecture is about an untwisted K3 category Db(S), not the weaker condition Ku(X) ≅ Db(S, α) for a twisted K3 surface. Your draft leaves this distinction implicit. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

If one wants the question completely self-contained, rational should be unpacked as K-rational, i.e. birational over K to P^4_K. This is implicit in the paper’s formulation rather than spelled out. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
refined_question: Let X ⊂ P^5_K be a smooth cubic hypersurface over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) ≠ 2, and let Ku(X) be the Kuznetsov component defined by the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H), O_X(2H)⟩, where H is the hyperplane class. Is X K-rational, i.e. birational over K to P^4_K, if and only if there exists an untwisted K3 surface S over K such that Ku(X) is K-linearly equivalent, as an exact triangulated category, to Db(S), the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on S? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic fourfolds in Section 7.2, nor at the birational categorical Torelli question. It is aiming at the rationality-versus-K3-realizability statement, and the survey states that exact problem in Section 3.4 as Conjecture 3.16, explicitly tying it to Kuznetsov’s original Conjecture 1.1. The nearby context on the same page supplies the needed setup: what a cubic fourfold is, the field assumption, and the definition of Ku(X) via the semiorthogonal decomposition. Remark 3.17 is essential for sharpening the draft faithfully, because it separates the conjectural untwisted K3 condition Db(S) from the weaker twisted K3 phenomenon Db(S, α). By contrast, Theorem 7.7 concerns reconstructing X from an equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2) that commutes with degree-shift functors, and Question 7.8 asks whether Ku-equivalence implies birationality; these are adjacent but different problems. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))
